item.title: The Landscaper Who Hid His Victims In Planters
item.description: Toronto landscaper Bruce McArthur concealed seven victims’ remains in garden planters at a property where he worked. In 2019, he pleaded guilty to eight counts of first-degree murder and received life sentences with no parole eligibility for 25 years.

item.title: The Conflicting Records In Sean Daugherty’s Death
item.description: Sean Daugherty, 12, died in Yorktown, Virginia, in April 2022. His death was ruled a suicide, but hospital and autopsy records differed on whether he had a history of suicidal thoughts. His family disputed the ruling and sought an outside investigation.

item.title: Her Buried Backpack Held Items That Weren’t Hers
item.description: Nine-year-old Asha Degree vanished from North Carolina in 2000. Her backpack, discovered in 2001, contained a concert shirt and library book that weren’t hers. DNA evidence later prompted property searches, but Asha remains missing and no one has been charged.

item.title: Why Danny Masterson’s Victims Feared Going To Police
item.description: Danny Masterson’s victims said fear of Scientology retaliation delayed reporting him; the church denies discouraging crime reports. The former That ’70s Show actor was convicted of two rapes in 2023 and sentenced to 30 years to life. He maintains his innocence and has challenged the convictions.

item.title: Her Teenage Intern Wore A Wire To Expose Her
item.description: After Gregg Smart’s 1990 murder in New Hampshire, Pamela Smart’s teenage intern secretly recorded conversations that helped convict her. The school media coordinator received life without parole in 1991. A judge rejected her latest bid for a new trial in September 2026.

item.title: He Staged Her Suicide But Left A Sneaker Print
item.description: Actress and Waitress filmmaker Adrienne Shelly was killed in her Manhattan office in 2006. A sneaker print helped expose the staged suicide and led investigators to construction worker Diego Pillco. He pleaded guilty to first-degree manslaughter and received 25 years in prison in 2008.
